entries.title: 1.2 The Grim World
entries.flavour: The world of Heraldry Skirmish is a realm of old faiths, broken kingdoms, hungry roads, and colder bargains. Kings, princes, bishops, and warlords still raise banners over land they can barely hold. They fight over relics, tolls, doctrine, trade roads, salt, iron, and pride. Their victories are measured in burnt farms and new taxes. Their defeats are carried by peasants who never chose a side.
entries.direction: Two warlords' banners planted on either side of a burnt farmstead; a tax collector's cart and armed men in the yard while a peasant family flees down the lane.

entries.title: 1.3.1 The Fall
entries.flavour: No one agrees on what ended the world. That has not stopped anyone from blaming someone else.
entries.direction: The colossal broken head of an imperial statue lying half-buried in a ploughed field, a farmer and ox small beside it; nobody knows what toppled it.

entries.title: 1.3.2 The Six Climates of Ruin
entries.flavour: Beyond the walls, land has become allegiance. Expedition ledgers still say forest, city, cavern, ice, desert, and swamp. Survivors know better. They use older names. The shape of the world is plain enough to anyone who has walked it. The broken mountains run down its spine. The dead empire and its ruined cities sprawl across the eastern heart. The great forest spreads west to the salt-coast, the ice locks the north, the dunes burn in the south beyond the mountain passes, and the swamps drown the south-east where the rivers give out at the sea. The old imperial roads still join all of it, straight and patient, running out from the Ashlands to every climate that survived. A dry label cannot warn a traveller that a road has memory, a court still sits without lungs, or a pool of black water may be listening.
entries.direction: A sweeping panorama from the spine of the broken mountains: western forest, eastern dead city, northern ice and southern dunes all visible at once under one sky; a lone surveyor with a staff in the foreground.

entries.title: The Greenmark
entries.flavour: The Greenmark is the great temperate forest of the surviving world. It is larger than the maps. Roots take a road within a season and make the mile-stones useless. Travellers report trees shifting at the edge of sight, upright hounds between trunks, and grove-circles where moss stays warm after snow. Foresters cut warning signs into bark for those who know how to read them. The most common sign means turn back even if the voice ahead is your own. The forest is no wilderness. It is a country that does not recognize human law.

entries.title: The Ashlands
entries.flavour: The Ashlands are the cities of the old empires after fire, law, and death finished with them. They sprawl across the eastern heart of the world, where the imperial roads still run out to every climate like spokes from a shattered wheel. Forums have collapsed into crypts. Temples lean over plazas filled with soot. Streets run black across districts no living guide will enter twice. Lamps still burn in shrines whose gods have no congregation. Patrols still cross boundaries that vanished before the current Bastions had names. The Ashlands are rich because whole treasuries died under stone. They are feared because the city still knows how to count.

entries.title: The Undermarches
entries.flavour: The Undermarches begin under every place that claims to have a foundation, and run deepest beneath the broken mountains at the world's centre. Mines break into older shafts. Older shafts open into tunnels no pick made. Surveyors return with maps that disagree with themselves. Wells sour overnight. Cellars breathe in winter. Borders on the surface mean little below, where passages run under rivers, burial hills, and walls the Bastions call secure. Down in the true dark the deep elves keep their own houses and their own law, older than any empire and crueller than any court that ever sat above. The deep does not need to invade. The surface keeps falling into it.

entries.title: The Pale City
entries.flavour: In the north, winter has become government. Cities that once held tens of thousands stand ice-locked, their gates frozen mid-closing. Towers crack in the cold. Courts, offices, processions, and taxes continue in forms no living citizen would recognize. Hearthhold sends parties north with oil, fire-charms, and instructions to leave tribute on the old road. No one agrees who first made that bargain. The snow covers ruin with clean hands. It heals nothing.

entries.title: The Sun-Drowned
entries.flavour: South of the broken mountains, the dunes have climbed over the wealthiest realms the world ever boasted of. Tomb-cities of the priest-kings break the horizon like teeth. Salt flats glitter where harbours stood. The desert leaves the dead in sight, enthroned, armoured, embalmed, or half-uncovered by wind. Saltspire's ledgers call the southern routes profitable. Its guides call them damned and charge for the difference. Under the sand, sealed courts keep their lamps lit.

entries.title: The Mire
entries.flavour: Where the southern rivers gave out before the sea, the swamps inherited the rest, spreading across the world's south-eastern lowlands. Bogs swallowed roads. Mangroves grew through village roofs. Stilt-houses lean over water that looks shallow until it opens. Reedmarch survives by toll, ferry, leechcraft, and denial. The hag-courts hold the deep fen, and they keep older bargains than any Bastion will admit to honouring. Everyone there knows The Mire is rising. No one profits from saying it aloud. The dead drift below the walkways. Sometimes they drift back.

entries.title: 1.3.3 The Six Bastions
entries.flavour: Each Bastion is a fortified holding: a walled town, a fortress-chapel, a sealed mining city, a stilt-town behind river-locks. None ruled before the Fall. They survived because they were small enough to be missed, lucky enough to be spared, or stubborn enough to close the gate while neighbours screamed outside. Now they are the great powers of what remains.
entries.direction: A great Bastion gate grinding shut at dusk, guards straining at the windlass inside while desperate figures outside reach for the closing gap.

entries.title: Greythorn
entries.flavour: Greythorn is a timber-walled town among ancient oaks at the last surviving crossroads of the western forest road. It endures because it pays the forest. Each autumn, tithe-bundles are left at the standing stones. Each spring, the gate-wardens count the foresters who returned, then count the tools of those who did not.

entries.title: Sablekeep
entries.flavour: Sablekeep is a fortified chapel-town built into the throat of a ruined imperial city, where the Ashlands meet the eastern edge of the forest and the old roads run straight on into the dead empire. It survives by burning. Consecrated braziers stand at every gate, bridge, and chapel window. They are never permitted to go out. The lower terraces rest on the bones of an older temple, and the bones are not all the right shape.

entries.title: Deepwarden
entries.flavour: Deepwarden is a sealed mining city carved into the foothills of the broken mountains. It survived the Fall by closing its great gate. Half the city was on the wrong side when it closed. The half that survived now lives in the upper terraces above what its people call simply the Dark.

entries.title: Hearthhold
entries.flavour: Hearthhold is a walled town in the high north, built around the Great Hearth that has burned without interruption since the Fall. If the Hearth goes out, Hearthhold dies: first the children, then the elderly, then everyone. Every resident takes a turn on the fire-watch. Children are taught to feed the flame before they are taught to read.

entries.title: Saltspire
entries.flavour: Saltspire is a tower-city built around a deep, sacred well at the centre of an oasis ringed by salt-pans and the bones of older cities. It has the only reliable water for a hundred miles. This makes it wealthy. It also makes it hated.

entries.title: Reedmarch
entries.flavour: Reedmarch is a stilt-town raised over log pilings on a network of barges, ferry platforms, and toll bridges. It is the only crossing for 30 miles in any direction. Its people are ferrymen, smugglers, apothecaries, leech-tenders, and corpse-haulers. They know what is buried under their floors. They prefer not to discuss it.

entries.title: 1.3.4 Magic in the Dying Lands
entries.flavour: The Five Traditions all survived the Fall. None survived intact.
entries.direction: A still life on a cracked altar: five damaged implements, one per tradition - a scorched spellbook, a chipped holy symbol, a bloodied ritual knife, a withered antler-and-holly charm, and a cracked crystal - each broken in its own way.

entries.title: 1.3.5 Monstrous Threats
entries.flavour: The Monsters of the Dying Lands are not scattered obstacles. They hold the world now. They keep roads closed, fields empty, shrines silent, and old borders meaningless. A village may vanish because of hunger, tax, fever, or weather. Outside the walls, those causes often have claws, banners, laws, or names.
entries.direction: An abandoned village street: claw-torn doors, an empty well, and a crude monster banner planted where the market cross once stood.

entries.title: 1.3.6 Adventurers and the Road
entries.flavour: Adventurers exist because the Bastions need work done beyond the reach of soldiers.
entries.direction: A small party walking out of a Bastion's postern gate along a muddy road, past a gibbet and a weathered warning post, toward a dark forest edge.

entries.title: 1.3.7 Legends and Echoes
entries.flavour: The Dying Lands remember. They do not remember kindly.
entries.direction: A barrow field at dusk where faint ghostly warriors of an ancient battle re-enact their last charge through the living grass, drawn only in sparse fine lines.

entries.title: Human
entries.flavour: Humans are short-lived strivers who raise fragile things in a brutal world and call the result civilization. They learn fast, adapt faster, and persist in places that wear steadier peoples down to nothing.
entries.direction: A human traveller of a Bastion in layered road clothes with a pack, walking staff and short sword; ordinary, weathered and determined.

entries.title: Halfling
entries.flavour: Halflings keep to hearth smoke and hidden roads, and to the quiet wisdom of staying alive while larger folk blunder into the dark. They are small and quick, and far harder to break than strangers ever expect.
entries.direction: A halfling traveller in a hooded cloak with a sling, a well-kept pack and a cooking pot, alert and capable.

entries.title: Dwarf
entries.flavour: Dwarves are cut from sealed stone halls, old grudges, and craft traditions older than most fallen kingdoms. Hardship did not sour them so much as harden them, and little in this world meets one of them head-on and walks away whole.

entries.title: Elf
entries.flavour: Elves are shaped by older forests and longer memories, and carry a grace that seems almost inhuman to the hurried peoples of the age. They move lightly, notice much, and bear the weight of beauty and loss without letting it show.
entries.direction: An elf traveller, tall and lean, in a long weathered cloak with a longbow and quiver, calm and watchful.

entries.title: Gnome
entries.flavour: Gnomes hold that every lock, mechanism, and buried device hides a lesson, and that the lesson is usually worth the risk of learning it. They are clever and precise, drawn to the exact dangers that sensible folk step around.
entries.direction: A gnome traveller with tinkering tools and lenses on a bandolier, a small crossbow and a heavy satchel.

entries.title: Goblin
entries.flavour: Goblins learn fast hands and quicker feet, and the plain truth that the weak survive by being where the blow is not. They fight mean, flee smart, and take every edge a hard world leaves lying about.
entries.direction: A goblin adventurer in a Bastion's employ: patched but well-kept leathers, a short blade and lantern, wary intelligence in the face; clearly a hired hero, not a raider.

entries.title: Orc
entries.flavour: Orcs are raised where weakness is punished at once and hesitation is never forgotten. Strength, momentum, and raw nerve have carried them this far, and they trust those three further than they trust subtlety.
entries.direction: An orc adventurer in a Bastion's employ: heavy travel-worn armour, a greataxe slung, scarred but composed; a sworn hireling, not a raider.

entries.title: Ratkin
entries.flavour: Ratkin come up from refuse heaps, tunnel warrens, and plague-alleys where numbers, speed, and hunger settled every argument. They know how to scatter, swarm, and strike where the enemy is already bleeding.
entries.direction: A ratkin adventurer in a hooded cloak and Bastion tabard, satchel of scavenged tools, bright watchful eyes; a hired hero, not a scavenger.

entries.title: Deep Elf
entries.flavour: Deep elves are a crueller branch of the elder blood, raised on night, venom, and treachery taught as a fine art. They are graceful and dangerous, and far more at ease beneath the dark than beneath the sun.
entries.direction: A deep elf adventurer who has come to the surface: pale skin, a hood pulled against daylight, fine dark armour and a curved blade; an outcast hireling, not a warrior of the deep courts.

entries.title: Demonborn
entries.flavour: Something infernal stains the demonborn line, whether by old pact, curse, or ancestral trespass. Doors do not open for them, but fire parts, fear bends, and darker powers sometimes answer when they are called.
entries.direction: A demonborn traveller with small horns, a tail and ember-like eyes, dressed in a plain pilgrim's cloak.

entries.title: Drakeblood
entries.flavour: The drakeblood carry the remnant of an older majesty in the blood, as blessing, burden, or half-remembered debt. The world is fallen, but power still answers them in the old language of flame, storm, and scale.
entries.direction: A drakeblood traveller with scaled skin along jaw and hands and a ridge of small horns, in a heavy cloak with a spear.

entries.title: Farmer
entries.flavour: A farmer grows up with callused hands, stubborn habits, and the certain knowledge that work hurts and stops for no one. Hard ground built them a thicker frame than most wandering blades will ever earn.

entries.title: Nomad
entries.flavour: A nomad crosses hard country under open skies, surviving where the roads fail and shelter is never promised. The land that grinds others down only taught them its lessons.

entries.title: Sailor
entries.flavour: A sailor learns balance on wet planks and danger under bad skies, shaped by rope, spray, and labour that does not wait on the weather. They keep their feet and keep moving while steadier folk go down.

entries.title: Soldier
entries.flavour: A soldier marched where they were told and fought when they were ordered, and learned that discipline keeps people alive longer than courage alone. War has settled into them now, and sits easy on the shoulders.

entries.title: Smuggler
entries.flavour: A smuggler lives by false bottoms, whispered routes, and the craft of keeping valuable things out of dangerous hands. Stealth is not a flourish to them. It is the trade that buys supper.

entries.title: Courier
entries.flavour: A courier carried news, coin, or secrets across broken roads and worse weather, for patrons who paid for speed and asked no questions. Speed was never a convenience. It was the difference between arriving and being found later.

entries.title: Scout
entries.flavour: A scout lived ahead of the line, where a broken branch or a fresh print decided whether the column ate or buried. They read ground, distance, and silence better than most people read letters.

entries.title: Performer
entries.flavour: A performer survived on wit, nerve, and the knack of making a crowd look where they wanted. Stage, tavern, or market square, they learned how attention is turned into a weapon.

entries.title: Artisan
entries.flavour: An artisan spent years making useful things with patient hands and a careful eye. The craft taught them the worth of good tools and good steel, and of work done properly the first time, because a second time is rarely offered.

entries.title: Scholar
entries.flavour: A scholar lived among books, diagrams, and arguments, and the stubborn belief that knowledge matters even in a dying world. Where others see only rubble, they read the record of how it came to fall.

entries.title: Apprentice
entries.flavour: An apprentice served beneath someone wiser, crueller, or more dangerous than themselves, and took what scraps of the craft they could. Even unfinished training leaves marks that never quite fade.

entries.title: Alchemist
entries.flavour: An alchemist learned that fire, acid, tincture, and powder solve problems steel cannot reach. Their satchel never quite loses the smell of copper, ash, and the next mistake.

entries.title: Believer
entries.flavour: A believer kept faith in a world that rewards it rarely, and learned that courage spreads as readily as panic. People stand straighter when they believe something is still watching from above.

entries.title: Hermit
entries.flavour: A hermit withdrew from the world, or was left behind by it. Silence, hunger, and long solitude taught them to listen for older truths and to depend on no one.

entries.title: Cultist
entries.flavour: A cultist served a darker altar once, out of terror, conviction, or need. Whatever they walked away from, part of it still answers when blood is spilled.

entries.title: Shepherd
entries.flavour: A shepherd watched helpless things for long hours and learned how predators move, wait, and choose. The surest way to live is to be the least tempting thing in the field.

entries.title: Merchant
entries.flavour: A merchant learned value, leverage, and the quiet power of knowing what desperate people will pay. Coin is never only money to them. It is movement, influence, and another season behind the walls.

entries.title: Noble
entries.flavour: A noble was raised among banners, debts, and inherited expectation. The fortune may be broken now, but privilege leaves marks the world is slow to forget.

entries.title: Pauper
entries.flavour: A pauper came up from the bottom, where every crust and every coin had to be fought for. Want made them wiry, stubborn, and stubbornly hard to finish.

entries.title: Vagabond
entries.flavour: A vagabond drifted from road to road with no roots deep enough to hold them anywhere. Luck, instinct, and shameless persistence carried them further than skill alone ever should have.

entries.title: Fighter
entries.flavour: A Fighter is forged in places where hesitation gets people killed. Drill, repetition, and hard lessons carve in the instinct to hold ground when holding it is the only thing that matters. They have watched lines collapse, and they know to the heartbeat how long one can stand before it does.

entries.title: Berserker
entries.flavour: A Berserker learned early that restraint is no shield. Pain becomes familiar, then distant, until nothing is left in the noise but the fight itself. When the violence starts, they meet it with nothing held back.

entries.title: Rogue
entries.flavour: A Rogue is bred in scarcity, where chances come rarely and are never handed over. Locks, shadows, and blind corners become tools long before anyone calls them a trade. A Rogue learns to take what is needed and be elsewhere before the loss is noticed.

entries.title: Assassin
entries.flavour: An Assassin is built on patience and certainty. They watch, wait, and act only when the outcome is assured. Most fights are avoided. The rest are ended quickly.

entries.title: Ranger
entries.flavour: A Ranger is schooled by ground that kills the careless. Tracks, wind, and distance tell them what others miss entirely. They learn to act before danger closes the gap, and to strike from where the enemy cannot answer.

entries.title: Cleric
entries.flavour: A Cleric keeps the faith long after letting it go would be easier. They have knelt in the silence where an answer should be and spoken the words anyway. Now and then something answers, and that is reason enough to kneel again.

entries.title: Paladin
entries.flavour: A Paladin is bound to a promise that does not bend, in an age that breaks promises for sport. Oaths weigh more than steel, and keeping one costs more than strength. Most let theirs go. A Paladin does not.

entries.title: Wizard
entries.flavour: A Wizard is formed through study that most would not endure. Fragments of knowledge, careful notes, and repeated failure shape their craft. Power is taken apart, understood, and rebuilt with precision.

entries.title: Psion
entries.flavour: A Psion turns inward until thought itself sharpens into a weapon, paring away everything that does not serve. What others fight to hold steady, a Psion bends to plain intent. The discipline is not so much chosen as survived.

entries.title: Trickster
entries.flavour: A Trickster survives by shaping what others take for true. Fact matters less than belief, and belief can be steered. They learn to move freely through the confusion they have already laid down.

entries.title: Sorcerer
entries.flavour: A Sorcerer is handed power they never asked to carry. It comes fast and demands to be spent, and left to fester it consumes the one who holds it. Spent well, it can settle everything in a single breath.

entries.title: Druid
entries.flavour: A Druid knows the world was never owned by those who built upon it. Stone cracks, root spreads, and time takes everything back into the dark soil. A Druid has seen that plainly, and chosen to serve it rather than resist it.

entries.title: 7.6 Treasure Tables
entries.flavour: Treasure in the Dying Lands is never clean. Coin comes from burial hoards, failed relief columns, chapel vaults, drowned roads, damned shrines, dead merchants, broken armies, and rooms sealed by people who feared being found. A purse is often the last record of a life. A crown may have passed through dirt, blood, ash, salt water, and another thief's stomach before it reaches a living hand.
entries.direction: A still life of grim treasure: a rotted purse spilling tarnished coins beside a skeletal hand, a mud-caked crown, a cracked reliquary and a salt-crusted signet ring.

entries.title: 7.8 Melee Weapons
entries.flavour: Many of the arms below carry names from an older, wider world than the Bastions now remember: the long-bladed messer, the notched swordbreaker, the throwing cross, the bladed scourge, the weighted cord, and the hook-and-chain. They reach the Dying Lands as salvage, tribute, and trade goods, carried up the southern routes through Saltspire and bartered onward through Reedmarch. How a blade is named changes nothing about how it cuts. Each is listed here under the name the traders used.
entries.direction: A still life of salvaged arms laid on sacking: a long-bladed messer, a notched swordbreaker, a throwing cross, a bladed scourge, a weighted cord and a hook-and-chain.

entries.title: Tier 1 Arcane Spells (d20)
entries.flavour: The first lessons any surviving academy still teaches: force, fire, and the manipulation of what the eye reports. Apprentices roll for what their masters had time to pass on.
entries.direction: A young apprentice at a scarred practice post conjuring a small flame in one hand while a shimmer of force bends the air before the other.

entries.title: Tier 2 Arcane Spells (d20)
entries.flavour: Beyond the apprentice work lie the spells that bent the old empire's wars. Each was copied from a library that has since burned.
entries.direction: A wizard hurriedly copying a spell from a scorched tome by candlelight while the library behind them burns.

entries.title: Tier 3 Arcane Spells (d20)
entries.flavour: These are the spells the towers killed to keep. What a wizard recovers at this tier, they recover from ash, ciphers, and the dead.
entries.direction: A wizard sifting ash and cipher-scraps among robed corpses on the floor of a ruined tower, a sealed book clutched to their chest.

entries.title: Tier 1 Divine Prayers (d20)
entries.flavour: The plainest mercies the surviving faiths can still call down: light, mending, and the courage to stand one more round.
entries.direction: A priest raising a lantern whose light falls on a wounded soldier, the wound visibly knitting closed.

entries.title: Tier 2 Divine Prayers (d20)
entries.flavour: Prayers answered less often and at greater cost. The gods that remain are listening, but they are tired, and they keep accounts.
entries.direction: A weary cleric kneeling at a cracked roadside shrine beside a ledger of offerings, candles guttering.

entries.title: Tier 3 Divine Prayers (d20)
entries.flavour: At this height a prayer is not asked but demanded, and something always answers. Whether it is the god prayed to is a question the devout do not raise aloud.
entries.direction: A priest with arms raised on a hilltop, demanding, as a vast ambiguous shape takes form in the storm clouds above.

entries.title: Tier 1 Sorceries (d20)
entries.flavour: Sorcery does not study. It bleeds. These first workings cost little blood and never fail, which is how they teach the unwary to want more.
entries.direction: A close view of a sorcerer's cut palm, drops of blood rising and twisting into a small crackling spark.

entries.title: Tier 2 Sorceries (d20)
entries.flavour: The price climbs with the power. A sorcerer who reaches this tier has already learned what their veins are worth and decided it a fair trade.
entries.direction: A gaunt sorcerer with scar-laddered forearms channelling a crackling storm between their hands.

entries.title: Tier 3 Sorceries (d20)
entries.flavour: The workings here do not care whether the caster survives them. Sorcerers who command this tier are counted among the things other people pray against.
entries.direction: A sorcerer half-consumed by their own working, a vortex of force tearing up the ground, villagers praying on their knees at a safe distance.

entries.title: Tier 1 Druidic Rituals (d20)
entries.flavour: The oldest circles teach these first: the small agreements with root, weather, and beast that the Greenmark still honours.
entries.direction: A druid kneeling with one palm pressed to an exposed root, a hare and a crow watching, rain beginning to fall.

entries.title: Tier 2 Druidic Rituals (d20)
entries.flavour: Here the rituals stop asking the wild for favours and begin speaking its language. The forest answers in kind, and not always gently.
entries.direction: A druid speaking aloud as the surrounding trees bend toward them and roots heave up out of the earth.

entries.title: Tier 3 Druidic Rituals (d20)
entries.flavour: At this tier a druid no longer borrows from the living world. They become a clause in its oldest contract, and the world keeps its terms.
entries.direction: A druid half-merged with an ancient oak, bark creeping over their skin and branches rising like antlers from their head.

entries.title: Tier 1 Psychic Abilities (d20)
entries.flavour: The first disciplines of the unquiet mind: to push, to read, to hold a thought steady where the world wants it scattered.
entries.direction: A psion seated with closed eyes, pebbles hovering in a slow ring around them and a candle flame standing perfectly still.

entries.title: Tier 2 Psychic Abilities (d20)
entries.flavour: Deeper into the self than most minds are built to go. Each ability here leaves a mark the psion learns to hide.
entries.direction: A psion alone in a dark corridor, hiding a trembling hand, fine cracks of strain around their eyes.

entries.title: Tier 3 Psychic Abilities (d20)
entries.flavour: At this tier the boundary between thought and world thins to nothing. What the psion imagines, the battlefield is briefly obliged to believe.
entries.direction: A psion on a battlefield where stone steps and a wall rise from nothing at their gaze, enemies stumbling as the ground obeys the psion's thought.

entries.title: Giant Tarantula
entries.flavour: A hand-span of bristled legs around a body the size of a war helm, the giant tarantula stalks the Greenmark's leaf litter on stilted, deliberate steps. Its fangs weep a venom that turns a victim's muscles to wet rope. It spins no snares, preferring to run prey down and pin it where it falls. Foragers keep one eye on the canopy, because the largest specimens hunt from above and drop.

entries.title: Goblin
entries.flavour: Knee-high, green-grey, and all elbows and malice, goblins infest the Greenmark's ruined steadings in chittering mobs. Each carries a notched blade and a sling of river stones, and not one will hold a line once the fight turns against it. Singly they are cowards; in numbers they are a tide. Greythorn's gate-wardens read goblin-sign in the chewed bones left along the road.
entries.direction: A Greenmark goblin raider with a notched blade and river-stone sling, part of a mob; hunched and malicious.

entries.title: Beastman
entries.flavour: All fur and grievance, a beastman is a hunched man-shape topped with the head of a goat or boar, its hands ending in black claws. They run the forest edge in warbands, raiding for meat and metal, and there is nothing in them that will parley. They were among the first things the burning years shaped, and they have bred true down every generation since.

entries.title: Bandit
entries.flavour: Not every threat in the Greenmark has claws. Bandits are deserters, broken tithe-collectors, and folk the Bastions could no longer feed, gathered under whichever of them is cruellest that season. They favour shortbows from cover and blades up close, and they fight dirtiest against anything already bleeding. A full purse or a good pauldron is reason enough.

entries.title: Satyr Reveler
entries.flavour: Goat-legged and laurel-crowned, the satyr reveler capers at the edge of the firelight, piping on something that was never carved from wood. The music is the weapon: it floods a listener with borrowed terror or walks them gently into the dark. Satyrs were fey once, before the long silence soured them, and their revels end now in shallow graves.

entries.title: Briarling
entries.flavour: A knot of animate thornwood the size of a hound, the briarling scuttles on root-claws with a low, dry rustle, and bursts in a spray of barbed splinters when it is cut down. They cluster in the deep groves the Antlered Warden keeps, spent freely as the forest's first and least-mourned line. Fire is the only sure answer to them.

entries.title: Dire Wolf
entries.flavour: Bigger than a pony at the shoulder, scarred and yellow-eyed, the dire wolf works the Greenmark in coordinated packs, cutting prey from the herd with grim patience. One is dangerous; a pack is a sentence on any lone traveller. They take the slow, the young, and the foolish, in that order. Greythorn's outriders do not ride alone in wolf season.

entries.title: Orc
entries.flavour: Broad as a doorway and built around a greataxe, the orc is the Greenmark's most disciplined raider, grey-skinned and heavy-jawed, its lower tusks jutting above a wall of shields. Where beastmen break, orcs hold their formation. A warband takes a steading methodically, gate by gate, and savours the hard fight more than the loot it wins.
entries.direction: An orc raider of the Greenmark with crude trophies and a notched cleaver, mid-snarl, nothing like a sworn hireling.

entries.title: Bugbear
entries.flavour: Seven feet of shaggy, long-armed menace with a flat face and fur the colour of dead bracken, the bugbear moves through the undergrowth in a silence it has no right to. It strikes from arm's reach before its quarry knows it is there, rising out of cover with a spiked morningstar already swinging. It much prefers the ambush to the open fight. Where bugbears lair, goblins serve as their terrified scouts.

entries.title: Harpy
entries.flavour: Half-mortal and half-carrion-bird, the harpy nests in the Greenmark's broken towers and sings travellers off the road and into its talons. The song is a lure that no resolve fully shakes. Up close it is filth and hooked claws, shrieking as it rakes. Its hunger is older than the Fall, and it was never once satisfied.

entries.title: Goblin Shaman
entries.flavour: Hung with fetishes of bone and crow-feather, the goblin shaman is the one goblin its own kind fears more than the enemy. It hangs behind the mob and spits hexes that wither courage and rot resolve. Its magic is small and spiteful, scavenged from older powers it does not begin to understand. Kill it, and the warband's nerve tends to break with it.

entries.title: Bandit Captain
entries.flavour: The bandit captain held a real commission once, or says so often enough to be believed. Armoured in looted mail and barking orders a crew will actually follow, they turn a rabble into something that fights like soldiers. They parry the first blow, answer the second, and spend their underlings freely to keep their own skin whole. Greythorn carries a standing bounty on three of them by name.

entries.title: Dire Bear
entries.flavour: The dire bear is the Greenmark grown teeth, a shaggy mountain of muscle that stands twice a man's height and swats deadwood aside to reach whatever it has smelled. It mauls with both forepaws and finishes with a bite that splits shields. Hunters who corner one rarely walk home. It bears no malice; it is only enormous, and always hungry.

entries.title: Blood Ape
entries.flavour: Slab-shouldered and crimson-furred, the blood ape knuckles through the high canopy and drops onto anything that bleeds. It fights in a building frenzy, both fists hammering faster as its own wounds mount, so the redder it grows the harder it hits. They hold the upper branches of the deep Greenmark and suffer no rival to share them.

entries.title: Gorebeak Bear
entries.flavour: Body of a bear, head and foreclaws of a great owl, the gorebeak is a stitched-together horror of the deep wood, its hooked beak punching clean through plate. It pins prey with raking claws and worries at the gap until something gives. Whether the burning years made these or merely woke them, the foresters cannot agree. The argument is no comfort to the pinned.

entries.title: Ogre
entries.flavour: Twice a man's height and slope-shouldered, an ogre is a slab of grey muscle and gut bound in stitched hides. It claims a ford or a narrow run between the trees and takes a toll of all that try to pass. It does not count coin. It counts the heavy, bright things its last few meals were carrying, and swings a tree-trunk club to collect more.

entries.title: Dryad Grovewarden
entries.flavour: Bark-skinned and crowned in living branches, a dryad grovewarden is the will of an old tree given a shape that can walk and a grudge it can hold. It steps between trunks as though they were doorways and binds intruders in grasping root. The Antlered Warden's tithe keeps most groves quiet. Where it goes unpaid, the grovewardens stir.

entries.title: Forest Troll
entries.flavour: Gangling, moss-slick, and stinking of the bog-edge, the forest troll is all reaching arms and a mouth of broken tusks. Its wounds knit shut before the blood has dried, and only fire or acid puts one down to stay. It is stupid, relentless, and forever hungry. Greythorn's woodcutters carry oil for exactly one reason.

entries.title: Werewolf
entries.flavour: A haunted villager by day, a hunched grey killer at the turning of need, the werewolf carries an old curse in its blood. Mundane steel slides from its hide; only silver and magic bite true. It strikes from the treeline and is gone before the screaming stops, then circles back for the wounded. Every bitten survivor is tomorrow's werewolf.

entries.title: Green Dragon
entries.flavour: Apex predator of the Greenmark and its oldest liar, the green dragon is a serpentine tyrant the colour of deep moss, spine-crested, its breath a rolling, corrosive poison. It does not rampage; it manipulates, ruling a swathe of forest through fear and bargain. Lesser things bring it tribute in exchange for being spared a while longer.
entries.direction: A typical adult green dragon of its kind, alone, coiled on a mossy rock; no lair, no tribute.

entries.title: Undead Warrior
entries.flavour: The Ashlands never disbanded its legions; it merely let them die unburied. An undead warrior is a skeleton or half-rotted corpse in the rusted kit of the old empire, still holding the post it was set to generations back. It fights in ragged ranks, shield to shield, mindless but drilled by sheer habit. There are always more of them in the ash.
entries.direction: A half-rotted corpse, not a bare skeleton, in rusted imperial legion kit with a short sword and a rectangular shield, ash underfoot.

entries.title: Undead Crossbowman
entries.flavour: Behind the shambling battle-line stand the crossbowmen, dead marksmen cranking warped windlasses with fleshless fingers. They loose in volleys at whatever their soldiers have fixed in place, and their bolts seek the gaps in armour with horrible patience. They do not tire, flinch, or lose their nerve. Only their bolts run out, eventually.

entries.title: Ghoul
entries.flavour: Grey, gaunt, and hook-clawed, a ghoul is what hunger makes of a corpse that would not lie still. It lopes in packs through the Ashlands' tombs, and its bite carries a paralytic rot that stiffens the limbs. Ghouls take the living and the freshly dead alike, and they are clever enough to cut off the straggler. They were people once, before the long famine that came after the cities burned.

entries.title: Possessed Corpse
entries.flavour: Not all the Ashlands' dead rose by design. A possessed corpse is a body worn by something that crept in from the dark between worlds, lurching on borrowed legs toward a wrong, jerking purpose. Its grip does not tire, and it bursts in a reek of corruption when it finally falls. Whatever rides it does not speak. It only reaches.

entries.title: Ember Skull
entries.flavour: A single charred head wreathed in green flame, the ember skull drifts the ruins on a cold updraft of malice, lighting the dark with its own hateful glow. It spits gouts of fire at the living from beyond their reach. Old grimoires name them the failed apprentices of the empire's pyromancers, kept burning by their final spite. Snuff the flame and the skull drops inert.

entries.title: Wererat
entries.flavour: Where the Ashlands meet the old sewers and undercrofts, the wererat thrives, a hunched, plague-grey shapeshifter scurrying between man and rat-thing. It bites, then skitters back into the dark, leaving filth-fever in every wound. Mundane blades barely mark it. One wererat is a nuisance; a nest of them is an outbreak.

entries.title: Spectre
entries.flavour: Grief and rage with the body burned away, a spectre drifts the Ashlands trailing the manner of its death. It passes through wall and armour alike, and its touch drinks the warmth and the years out of the living. Steel finds nothing to bite; only silver and magic answer. The ruined city is thick with them, each one a question that was never answered.

entries.title: Undead Sentinel
entries.flavour: They guarded the empire's gates in life and they guard the rubble of them in death, towering dead men in tower-shield and reach-halberd. A sentinel plants itself in a breach and will not be shifted, lending its iron stillness to the lesser dead around it. It does not pursue. It only holds, forever, a line that fell centuries ago.
entries.direction: A towering gaunt dead soldier planted in a broken gateway, rusted tower-shield grounded and reach-halberd raised.

entries.title: Undead Champion
entries.flavour: Raised from the largest corpses the Ashlands could muster, the undead champion is a slab of dead muscle swinging a maul of fused bone. Each blow lands with siege-engine weight and rattles whatever stands beside the thing it struck. It is slow, single-minded, and almost impossible to put off its feet. Where it walks, the lesser dead come on in its wake.

entries.title: Gargoyle
entries.flavour: By daylight a gargoyle is nothing but one more of the empire's stone guardians, perched and patient on a broken cornice. Let prey stray beneath, and the stone splits into claws and a biting maw. Its hide turns aside all but the heaviest blow. The Ashlands bristle with statues, and not every statue is one.

entries.title: Stone Sentinel
entries.flavour: A faceless construct of the old empire, the stone sentinel grinds forward on legs of carved granite and pounds with fists like falling masonry. It feels nothing and fears nothing, and it stops only when it is shattered. The empire raised thousands to guard halls that no longer stand. They guard them still.

entries.title: Minotaur
entries.flavour: Bull-headed and giant, the minotaur stalks the Ashlands' labyrinthine ruins and never once loses its way among the fallen streets. It charges head-down to gore and trample, then wades in with a greataxe. Its senses cut clean through smoke and shadow, so no ambush takes it in its own maze. Old maps mark its haunts with a single horned skull.

entries.title: Night Hag
entries.flavour: A withered crone of the between-places, the night hag slips into the waking world to feed on fear and curse the sleeping. Their claws leave a wound that festers, and when a fight turns against them they step half into the ether and are gone. They bargain, they lie, and they curse the young from the shadows. The Ashlands' long nights are their hunting ground.

entries.title: Forsaken Archer
entries.flavour: The Forsaken were the empire's finest, sworn to an oath that outlived the flesh that swore it. A forsaken archer draws a cursed longbow with a dead marksman's precision, and its arrows leave a clinging curse where they strike. Smoke and shadow do not trouble its aim. It serves Captain Veyr still, exactly as it once swore it would.

entries.title: Forsaken Knight
entries.flavour: Dead chivalry in spectral plate, the forsaken knight advances through the ash with a flamberge wreathed in grave-light. It parries with a lifetime's drill written into bone and cannot be slowed or turned aside. Bound by an oath it can no longer recall, it follows Veyr's banner into every fight. Its honour has curdled into compulsion.

entries.title: Forsaken Duelist
entries.flavour: Faster than a dead thing has any right to be, the forsaken duelist fights with a single flashing rapier and a fencer's lethal economy. It waits for a blade to commit, slips the strike, and answers through the opening. In life it was the empire's finest fencer; in death it is the same, only tireless. Veyr keeps the duelists close, for they punish every misjudged swing.

entries.title: Basilisk
entries.flavour: Heavy and eight-legged and the size of an ox, the basilisk drags itself through the Ashlands' rubble behind a gaze that turns flesh slowly to stone. Meet its eyes and the stiffening starts, the limbs first, then the rest. Even its blood petrifies whatever it touches. The ruins are dotted with its leavings, statues of the surprised, caught mid-stride.

entries.title: Ashen Revenant
entries.flavour: An ashen revenant is a corpse-warrior in fire-blackened plate, risen with one purpose welded into its bones: to kill the thing that killed it. It hunts that grudge across the Ashlands with tireless focus, and struck down it claws upright again to land a final blow. Cross its path and you become the grudge. It does not stop until you do.

entries.title: Iron Golem
entries.flavour: The empire's master-smiths forged iron golems to outlast the dynasty, and in that one task they grimly succeeded. A towering automaton of riveted black iron, it shrugs off blade and spell alike and answers with piledriver fists. Magic washes from its plates; edged steel skids away. It guards a throne whose claimant is centuries of dust.

entries.title: Lich
entries.flavour: A lich is an archmage who refused death and paid for the refusal in everything that made them human. A desiccated sorcerer-king in mouldering finery, they command the Ashlands' dead with a gesture and loose blasts of soul-rending necrosis. Destroy the body and they re-form, so long as the hidden phylactery endures. The empire fell. Its worst survivor did not.

entries.title: Kobold
entries.flavour: Knee-high reptilian scavengers with dull scales and dingy picks, kobolds are the Undermarches' scuttling vermin-folk. One alone is nothing; a chittering mob of them, dragging traps and loosing slings from the dark, is a real danger. They know every tunnel and trust not one. Where a single kobold shows itself, a whole warren is watching.

entries.title: Cave Goblin
entries.flavour: Paler and blinder than their forest cousins, cave goblins have gone so long without sun that their eyes are wide black pools. They jab with jagged spears and bolt at the first hint of a losing fight. They infest the upper deep in nervous packs. A cave goblin's first instinct is to flee toward more cave goblins.

entries.title: Giant Bat
entries.flavour: Leathery-winged and wider than a man is tall, the giant bat navigates the lightless depths by shrieks no living ear can catch. It harries intruders in swooping passes, biting and wheeling away before the answer lands. Torchlight only draws more of them. Whole colonies hang in the upper caverns, and they wake all at once.

entries.title: Vaultfang
entries.flavour: A vaultfang clings to the cavern roof as a flawless imitation of a stalactite, a mottled cone of stone-hard chitin, and it waits. When something passes beneath, it drops, driving its single barbed point clean through helm and skull. It is a living spear that falls exactly once. Few who survive a low ceiling here ever walk easy under one again.

entries.title: Giant Centipede
entries.flavour: Many-segmented and as long as a spear, the giant centipede pours over cave walls on a hundred legs, mandibles dripping a venom that locks the muscles solid. It hunts by vibration in the lightless dark. A bite swells black within minutes. Its shed husks carpet the floors of the oldest tunnels.

entries.title: Noxcloth
entries.flavour: The noxcloth hangs from the cavern roof like a fold of black leather the size of a flung cloak, no different from shadow until it drops to smother. It wraps a victim's head and crushes, blind itself but needing no eyes in the dark it brings with it. With a gout of unnatural gloom it can snuff a torch outright. Of all the things that wait on the deep's ceilings, it is the one to fear most.

entries.title: Troglodyte
entries.flavour: Grey, crested, and degenerate, troglodytes are reptilian cave-dwellers whose skin shifts colour to vanish against bare stone. They reek so violently that the stench alone sickens the unready. They hunt in clutches, claws first, fading in and out of the rock. Their territory announces itself by smell long before anything is seen.

entries.title: Giant Black Widow
entries.flavour: Glossy-black and the size of a war-hound, the giant black widow squats in a cathedral of its own webbing, the telltale crimson mark on its swollen back. It flings strands to snare prey from across a chamber, then closes to deliver a venom that stops the heart cold. They are the Broodmother's lesser daughters, and they spin the most lethal traps below.

entries.title: Gloomspore Jelly
entries.flavour: A translucent grey ooze the size of a cart, the gloomspore jelly creeps over every surface and dissolves whatever it engulfs. Slashing only splits it, and it feels neither pain nor fear. Destroyed at last, it bursts in a cloud of soporific spores. It leaves the tunnels behind it scoured clean and faintly glistening.

entries.title: Troglodyte Shaman
entries.flavour: The troglodyte shaman daubs itself in glowing fungus and mutters to things that dwell below even the deep. It calls up reeking clouds and spiteful hexes to soften prey for the clutch. Its magic is primitive but real, and older than any empire that ever named it. The other troglodytes give way before it, and so should anything wise.

entries.title: Vault Ooze
entries.flavour: Near-invisible and wall to wall, a vault ooze is a cube of acidic slime that fills a corridor and sweeps it clean of everything that ever breathed. The unwary walk straight in and are engulfed, dissolving while still aware of it. It moves in eerie silence, betrayed only by a faint shimmer. The neatest tombs in the deep were swept out by these.

entries.title: Vrymk
entries.flavour: A writhing tangle of stone-grey tentacles around a cruel hooked beak, no broader than a crouching man, the vrymk clings to cavern walls until prey wanders close. Camouflaged against the rock, it lashes out with rubbery arms and hauls the catch to its maw. It hunts by patience and ambush rather than speed. Anyone who hears a wet, slithering rasp from a bare wall has already been seen.

entries.title: Deep Elf Warrior
entries.flavour: The deep elves quit the surface ages before the Fall and have curdled, in the dark, into something coldly beautiful and merciless. A deep elf warrior fights with poisoned hand-crossbow and finesse blade, seeing perfectly in a lightlessness that blinds everything else. They raid the upper deep for slaves and for sport. Mercy was a surface weakness they bred out long ago.
entries.direction: A deep elf warrior of the deep courts in full dark ceremonial armour with a crescent glaive, in the Undermarches gloom.

entries.title: Deep Elf Priest
entries.flavour: Robed in black silk and bone fetishes, a deep elf priest serves the spider-gods of the deep. It wreathes its enemies in conjured darkness and bends their wills with a single spoken command. From the shadow it has made, scourge in hand, it drives the warriors forward. Its faith is cruelty refined into ritual.
entries.direction: A deep elf priest in layered dark vestments raising a shadow-wreathed sigil staff.

entries.title: Gloom Hulk
entries.flavour: Beetle-backed and the size of a bull, the gloom hulk is a digger armed with great scything claws and four eyes that scramble the mind of anything that meets them. It burrows through solid rock to erupt beneath its prey. Its gaze leaves victims reeling and helpless where they stand. More than one collapsed gallery in the deep is its doing.

entries.title: Cryptstrangler
entries.flavour: A cryptstrangler passes for a stalagmite taller than a man until its strands uncoil, a stony predator that flings sticky tendrils across a chamber, reels in the catch, and bites it through. It can sit motionless for years between meals. The tendrils come from angles no one expects, faster than anything that still should move. Not every silent column down here is only stone.

entries.title: Elder Vrymk
entries.flavour: Where lesser vrymk lurk as ambushers, the eldest of a brood swells to monstrous size. It is a knot of stone-grey tentacles thick as a man's leg, gathered around a beak that shears clean through plate. It no longer hunts alone; the smaller kin gather to its silent direction and drag prey within its reach. A tunnel scoured of every other living thing is its larder.

entries.title: Evil Eye
entries.flavour: A floating orb of leathery flesh ruled by one great central eye and crowned with writhing eyestalks, the evil eye spits a different doom from each lesser eye. It drifts the deep wrapped in an aura that unmakes magic outright. No two of its glares do the same thing twice. It regards every other living thing as a competitor to be erased.

entries.title: Burrowmaw
entries.flavour: An armour-plated horror the size of a wagon, the burrowmaw has a blunt head and a maw that splits its whole face open. It swims through solid stone and erupts beneath its prey in a shower of rubble. It senses footfalls through the rock and leaps the last span with its jaws spread wide. The stone trembles faintly before it surfaces, and that is the only warning anyone gets.

entries.title: Thought-Eater
entries.flavour: A robed, four-tentacled humanoid with an octopus's head, the thought-eater wears grey, slick skin and white, pupilless eyes. It feeds on living minds, and a single psychic blast drops a whole party to their knees. It can seize a victim's will and turn them on their own friends. It schemes in the dark beneath the dark, and to meet one is to feel it already reading you.

entries.title: Frozen Skeleton
entries.flavour: Rimed in blue frost, a sword welded to its hand by ice, a frozen skeleton is one of the Pale City's countless dead, still standing the post it was given. It guards avenues that have not seen a living census in centuries. The cold preserves it whole; it will hold that post when the last warm thing in the world goes out. There are always more under the snow.
entries.direction: A frost-rimed skeleton with icicles hanging from its ribs and a sword frozen to its hand, snow drifted around its feet.

entries.title: Snow Goblin
entries.flavour: Gaunt and white-furred, snow goblins den in the Pale City's drifts and tunnels, ambushing out of the whiteout with frost-edged knives. They are invisible against the snow until the moment they move. Cowardly and quick, they strip the frozen dead and bolt from any honest fight. The blizzard hides both their approach and their retreat.

entries.title: Ratkin Scavenger
entries.flavour: The ratkin are a verminous rat-folk that boiled up into the Pale City when the long winter first came down. The scavengers are their lowest caste, scrawny twitching things in matted grey fur, darting through the ruins to strip anything not frozen to the ground. They swarm, they scurry, and they rarely stand to fight. Where the scavengers pick, the warren is never far behind.

entries.title: Tundra Wolf
entries.flavour: White-coated and built for the killing cold, the tundra wolf pads across ice that would betray a heavier foot. It runs in packs that herd prey into the open, where the wind does half the killing. Its bite carries the chill of the Pale City itself. Travellers who hear no howling are in the gravest danger of all.

entries.title: Ratkin Warrior
entries.flavour: A hunched, spear-wielding rat-man in scavenged scraps of plate, the ratkin warrior fights shoulder to shoulder behind a bristling wall of points. Alone it falters; in a shield-rank it holds. The warren feeds them forward in chittering blocks. They die easily and breed faster than they die.

entries.title: White Court Guard
entries.flavour: The White Court is the Pale City's undead nobility, and the guard is its rank and file: a frost-armoured corpse bearing a reach-halberd, moving with the cold discipline of a court that never once adjourned. They lock shields across the frozen avenues and advance by the old drill. Death only made them more obedient.
entries.direction: A frost-armoured noble corpse in ornate courtly armour and a frozen fur mantle, reach-halberd held at a ceremonial slant.

entries.title: Ratkin Seer
entries.flavour: Draped in icicle-charms and half-mad, the ratkin seer spits frost-hexes that sap the warmth and the will from its enemies. It hangs behind the warriors, croaking prophecy and curse in the same breath. Its magic is scavenged and unreliable, but a hex that lands at the wrong moment still kills. The warren treats its ravings as law.

entries.title: Frost Ghoul
entries.flavour: A ghoul frozen and reborn in the Pale City's cold, its claws sheathed in killing frost and its hunger undimmed, the frost ghoul hunts in packs through the snow-choked streets. It drags down the living to feed. The cold that should still it only whets its appetite. It does not slow, and it does not stop while anything warm remains.

entries.title: White Court Archer
entries.flavour: From the frozen balconies of the dead city, white court archers loose volleys of ice-fletched arrows, dead marksmen whose aim outlasted the flesh that learned it. They mass their fire on whatever the soldiers have pinned. The cold steadies their hands more surely than any living discipline could. Their quivers never empty.

entries.title: Blackfire Hound
entries.flavour: Cold black flame guttering along its spine, the blackfire hound is a charred beast-shape that leaves a trail of smouldering ash across the snow. Its bite burns with a fire no ordinary frost-ward will stop. They course in packs through the Pale City's ruins, herding prey onto their own burning trails. The snow hisses where they pass.

entries.title: Ice Wraith
entries.flavour: A knife of frozen malice given a drifting, translucent shape, the ice wraith is the spirit of someone who froze to death in the Pale City and never forgave it. Its touch saps warmth and thickens the blood to sludge. Steel passes clean through; only silver and magic bite. It haunts the coldest avenues, hungry for the heat of anything still living.

entries.title: White Court Sentinel
entries.flavour: A greatshield-bearing corpse-knight, the white court sentinel is the dead nobility's bodyguard, planting itself before its lords and refusing to give ground. It lends its frozen resolve to the soldiers around it and weathers blows that would shatter a lesser guardian. It will not pursue and will not break. It only endures, as the court endures.
entries.direction: A corpse-knight crouched behind an enormous greatshield, ornate visored helm, no polearm.

entries.title: Ice Elemental
entries.flavour: A lurching figure of living glacier, jagged and groaning, the ice elemental freezes the ground it crosses and the limbs it lands upon. Its slamming fists lock muscle solid in an instant. Fire is its bane; frost means nothing to it. The Pale City's deep cold breeds them where the ice grows thick enough to dream.

entries.title: Fallen Paladin
entries.flavour: Holy oath turned to grave-frost, the fallen paladin is an undead knight in defiled plate, radiating an aura that withers the courage of all who come near. Its flamberge carries a necrotic chill, and despair leaks off it the way cold leaks off ice. It guards the Pale City's blackest chapels. Whatever vow it broke in life, it keeps a darker one now.

entries.title: Werebear
entries.flavour: In the Pale City's frozen wilds prowls the werebear, a hulking man-beast of white fur and ruinous strength, damned kin to the werewolf but built to maul rather than skirmish. It strikes with both paws and a bone-cracking bite, and hurls grown men aside. Mundane weapons barely part its hide. A single one can break a war-band.

entries.title: White Court Executioner
entries.flavour: The white court executioner carries out sentences the living court passed centuries ago, a towering headsman whose frost-rimed axe seeks the weakest throat on the field. It strides past the hale to reach the wounded and ends them with grim efficiency. The court's justice did not die with the court. It only grew patient.
entries.direction: A towering hooded headsman striding forward with a frost-rimed executioner's axe over one shoulder.

entries.title: Frost Wyvern
entries.flavour: A lesser cousin of the great dragons, the frost wyvern is a winged reptile the colour of dirty ice, a venom-and-frost sting whipping at the end of its tail. It stoops from the white sky to harry and poison, then climbs out of reach before the answer comes. It is cunning rather than wise. The Pale City's frozen peaks are crowded with their roosts.
entries.direction: A frost wyvern on the wing, two-legged and lean, distinctly smaller and rangier than a dragon.

entries.title: Gelid Fiend
entries.flavour: The Pale City's frozen law keeps advocates that were never born under any sun. A gelid fiend is summoned and bound into the cold, a towering devil of blue-white ice and cruel geometry, its hide a lattice of frozen carapace. It raises walls of ice to pen its quarry and enforces judgements no mortal court would dare to sign. It does not tire, bargain, or relent, and the cold around it is the cold of a sentence already handed down.

entries.title: Frost Giant
entries.flavour: Twice a man's height and blue-skinned, the frost giant goes armoured in glacier-ice and brings a greataxe down like an avalanche. It hurls boulders to scatter foes before it closes the distance. The Pale City's oldest streets were built to its scale, by something, for reasons no one living recalls. It rules the high drifts as a king.

entries.title: White Dragon
entries.flavour: The Pale City's frozen sovereign, the white dragon is a feral, ice-crusted wyrm whose breath flash-freezes whatever it touches. Less cunning than its kin but no less lethal, it is pure predatory cold given wings and an appetite. It nests in the highest spire and suffers the White Court about it as courtiers. When it descends, the city's eternal winter only deepens.
entries.direction: A typical adult white dragon, alone on a jagged ice outcrop with wings half-raised; no spire, no city.

entries.title: Fire Beetle
entries.flavour: Hard-shelled and the size of a dog, the fire beetle carries a ruddy inner heat that lights the tomb-passages it infests. It snaps with burning mandibles and bursts into a gout of flame when crushed. Tomb-robbers prize its glands for their steady light. The beetles prize the tomb-robbers for their meat.

entries.title: Imp
entries.flavour: Knee-high and bat-winged, a barbed venomous tail lashing behind it, the imp flits about the Sun-Drowned tombs as the spiteful servant of darker things. It darts in to sting and wheels away cackling, untroubled by the desert's heat or its own infernal fire. Alone it is more nuisance than threat. It is also a herald of worse to come.

entries.title: Skeleton Warrior
entries.flavour: A skeleton warrior stands at the post it was set in the year of its death, a sun-bleached frame in the corroded bronze of a priest-king's guard. It still holds the weapon it carried in life, waiting on an order that has not come in centuries. When intruders breach the sealed courts the order arrives at last, and the bones remember their drill. There are always more, ranked in the dark behind it.
entries.direction: A bare sun-bleached skeleton in corroded bronze scale and a crested bronze helm, holding a curved bronze blade, sand underfoot.

entries.title: Corpsehound
entries.flavour: Jackal-headed and quick, the corpsehound runs the dunes between man and beast, hunting the Sun-Drowned's caravans in loping packs. It strikes hardest off a running start, scimitar in one hand and slavering jaws beneath. They serve the tomb-courts as scouts and trackers. By the time the laughter reaches you, the pack already has your scent.

entries.title: Gnoll
entries.flavour: Hyena-headed, rangy, and ruled by a bottomless hunger, gnolls sweep out of the Sun-Drowned wastes to fall on anything weaker than themselves. A gnoll that drops a victim grows frenzied and surges straight on to the next. They take slaves and meat and leave the bones in the sand. Their cackling carries for miles in the dry air.

entries.title: Giant Scorpion
entries.flavour: The size of a cart and banded in chitin plate, the giant scorpion bears two crushing pincers and a venom-dripping sting arched above its back. It buries itself in the dunes and erupts beneath whatever walks over it. Its venom liquefies a body from within. The Sun-Drowned's sands hide thousands of them, each one waiting on a footfall.

entries.title: Skeleton Archer
entries.flavour: The archers of the priest-king tombs stand in alcoves carved to fit them, bows still strung after centuries. The arrows have not rotted; some things are kept by intention, others by spite. They loose in disciplined volleys at whatever the skeleton warriors have engaged. Their aim is exactly as good as it was the day they died.

entries.title: Mummy
entries.flavour: A priest-king's preserved corpse risen in wrath, the mummy comes bound in resin-soaked wrappings and trailing the dread of a dead god's authority. Its touch lays a withering curse, and the mere sight of it can root a victim in terror. Fire is its one true fear. It guards a tomb whose treasures it will not share, not even now.

entries.title: Skeletal Beast
entries.flavour: The bound remains of some great desert predator, the skeletal beast is a charging framework of fang and claw with nothing left in it to slow it down. It runs prey to ground across the open sand and tears with bony jaws. No flesh means no fatigue and no fear. The tomb-courts loose them like hounds.

entries.title: Wind Elemental
entries.flavour: A howling spiral of desert air turned malevolent, the wind elemental is a near-invisible vortex that flings sand and bodies with equal ease. It buffets foes off their feet and is barely troubled by ordinary weapons. It haunts the open wastes where the Sun-Drowned's storms are born. You hear it long before the sand begins to bite.

entries.title: Desert Naga
entries.flavour: A great serpent with an almost-human face and the patient cunning of something very old, the desert naga coils among the tomb-pillars. It spits venom from a distance and crushes what comes close, hexing the strong to leave them weak. The priest-kings kept them as guardians and oracles. They guard still. They no longer answer.

entries.title: Fire Elemental
entries.flavour: A roaring man-shape of living flame, white-hot at the core and shedding embers at the edges, the fire elemental sets alight everything it touches and scorches whatever strikes it. Water and ice are its only checks; the desert sun is its cradle. It draws a trail of cinders across the tomb-floors. To lay hands on it is to burn.

entries.title: Giant Skeleton
entries.flavour: A looming framework of fused bone twice a man's height, the giant skeleton is what remains of something that was never entirely natural and is far less so now. It moves with grinding deliberation, sweeping aside anything in its path with fists like falling masonry. Tomb-city carvings show its kind kneeling before the priest-kings; none show them standing. Whatever it was raised to guard, it guards it still.

entries.title: Medusa
entries.flavour: A serpent-haired figure whose gaze turns the living slowly to stone, the medusa lurks among the statues that were once its admirers. It fights with blade and venomous snake-hair, but its eyes are what fill the tomb-galleries with permanent witnesses. The priest-kings cursed its kind, or rewarded them; the tales cannot agree. Their victims cannot say.

entries.title: Tomb Necromancer
entries.flavour: The necromancers of the Sun-Drowned were the tombs' original administrators, robed officials who chose preservation over death and never gave up their posts. A tomb necromancer is a withered figure in the faded regalia of a dead bureaucracy, raising the buried to enforce statutes no living court remembers. It withers the living with a gesture and calls up the dead to fill the gaps in its ranks. Everything it administers belongs to a world that ended.

entries.title: Tomb Guardian
entries.flavour: A faceless construct of gilded stone and ritual, the tomb guardian was built to defend the priest-kings' seals and is tireless in that one duty. It plants itself at a threshold, lends its iron resolve to the dead around it, and cannot be hurried or frightened. It has held one doorway for a thousand years. It will hold it for a thousand more.

entries.title: Brass Golem
entries.flavour: A burnished automaton glowing with the trapped heat of the forge-rites that made it, the brass golem hammers with fists that sear on contact. Fire cannot harm it; it is fire's own child. The Sun-Drowned's wealthiest tombs are sealed behind these. They do not rust, tire, or reason.

entries.title: Manticore
entries.flavour: A monstrous fusion of lion's body, bat's wings, and a man's leering face, the manticore flicks volleys of iron spikes from its lashing tail. It waits where the dune-road narrows and rains barbs on whatever it has trapped. It savours a meal that begged first. The Sun-Drowned's loneliest trails are its larder.

entries.title: Demon
entries.flavour: A horned fiend the colour of cooling iron, wreathed in a flame that clings without consuming it, the demon clawed its way into the Sun-Drowned through some tomb-breached ward. It hews with a hooked glaive and looses surges of fire that pay no heed to armour. Those near it feel their courage drain away. Something summoned it once, and that something is almost certainly dead by now.

entries.title: Blue Dragon
entries.flavour: The Sun-Drowned's apex tyrant, the blue dragon is a horned, sand-scaled wyrm that burrows beneath the dunes and erupts amid its prey in a lance of lightning. Vain and territorial, it rules a swathe of desert and the tomb-courts caught within it. It hoards beneath the sand and surfaces only to feed or to punish. The static before its breath raises every hair on the body.
entries.direction: A typical adult blue dragon bursting up out of a dune, sand cascading from its horns.

entries.title: Bogling
entries.flavour: Squat and frog-mouthed, boglings lurk chest-deep in The Mire's reeking shallows with spears at the ready. They croak warnings across the water and hurl mud-darts before they close. Cowardly alone, they mass in the hundreds in the deep fens. The Mire's first warning is always the same: a sudden, total silence of frogs.

entries.title: Swamp Goblin
entries.flavour: Slime-streaked cousins of their forest kin, swamp goblins paddle The Mire's channels and blow poisoned darts from the reeds. They melt into the cover and strike from wherever the water hides them. A nuisance one at a time, a hazard in a swarm. They strip the drowned for trinkets and teeth.

entries.title: Zombie
entries.flavour: A waterlogged corpse that The Mire would not keep, the zombie lurches upright in tattered remains, driven by a single-minded hunger. It is slow and mindless and horribly hard to put down, shrugging off blows that would fell a living man. It drifts beneath the walkways until something warm passes overhead. Then it reaches up.

entries.title: Stirge
entries.flavour: A bloated mosquito-thing the size of a cat, the stirge carries a needle proboscis and a belly that swells red with stolen blood. It darts in, latches on, and drains until it is pried loose. The Mire's dusk air hums with them. One is an itch; a swarm is exsanguination.

entries.title: Will-o'-Wisp
entries.flavour: A drifting orb of pale corpse-light, the will-o'-wisp lures travellers off the safe paths and into the sucking mire to drown. It hangs motionless as a false beacon until prey strays near, then strikes with a shock of cold lightning. It feeds on the terror of the dying. The kindest-looking light in the mire is the one most likely to kill.

entries.title: Lizardfolk Warrior
entries.flavour: Scaled and cold-eyed, the lizardfolk warrior hunts The Mire as easily in the water as on the rotting banks, fighting with heavy club and javelin in disciplined packs. They are not cruel, only pragmatic; to them the living are meat and territory. They defend their breeding-pools without mercy. The mire is theirs, and they forget no intruder who enters it.

entries.title: Lizardfolk Hunter
entries.flavour: A barbed harpoon in its claws, the lizardfolk hunter stalks The Mire's margins, dragging prey off the walkways and into the water where every advantage is its own. It strikes from cover and the reeds, unseen until the line snaps taut. Patient and silent, it waits out the careless. By the time it moves, you are already in the water.

entries.title: Crocodile
entries.flavour: Grown to monstrous length in The Mire, the crocodile is a log-still ambusher that explodes from the murk to clamp on and drag its victim under in a death-roll. It can lie motionless for hours with only its eyes above the water. The deep channels belong to these. The walkways exist because of them.

entries.title: Lizardfolk Shaman
entries.flavour: Cloaked in dried reeds, the lizardfolk shaman speaks for the swamp-spirits, mending its packmates' wounds and hexing their prey. It hangs back among the warriors, croaking invocations over the water. Its magic is old and patient and bound to the mire itself. Kill the shaman and the pack fights harder, but it bleeds out faster.

entries.title: Miasma Serpent
entries.flavour: A bloated water-snake, the miasma serpent exhales clouds of poison gas as it swims, leaving a drifting green pall across the channels. Its bite carries a venom that festers fast. It hunts by lying in the haze of its own making. The mire's foulest-smelling stretches are where they nest.

entries.title: Swamp Naga
entries.flavour: A great serpent with a hooded, watchful face, the swamp naga coils among the drowned ruins, spitting venom and binding prey in its crushing length. It hexes the strong to sap their strength before it strikes. Older than the mire's human settlements, it remembers when the ground was dry. It guards sunken treasures no one else can reach.

entries.title: Giant Constrictor
entries.flavour: Long enough to bridge a channel, the giant constrictor drops from overhanging branches to coil and crush. It strikes, immobilizes, and squeezes the breath from its prey in the space of a few seconds. Then it slides back into the water before any rescue can reach it. The low branches over the mire are never safe to walk beneath.

entries.title: Shambling Mound
entries.flavour: A heaving mass of animate rot and creeper-vine, roughly man-shaped and utterly tireless, the shambling mound engulfs its prey in its sodden bulk. Lightning only feeds it; blades vanish into the muck. It drifts the deep fen absorbing whatever it smothers. The mire grows them wherever enough has drowned and rotted together.

entries.title: Swamp Hag
entries.flavour: A warty, weed-haired crone, the swamp hag poles their way through The Mire cursing all they meet, slipping half into the spirit-world when cornered. Their stench chokes out hope. They bargain, they lie, and they feed on misery. The loneliest hut in the mire is theirs, and it is never empty for long.

entries.title: Banshee
entries.flavour: The shrieking spirit of a woman drowned in grief, the banshee is a translucent horror whose wail stops hearts and freezes the blood. It drifts The Mire's fog, and its keening carries the plain certainty of death. Steel passes through it; only magic answers. To hear the wail clearly is to be the one it has chosen.

entries.title: Swamp Troll
entries.flavour: A slime-green giant of reaching arms and a tusked maw, the swamp troll hauls itself through The Mire on all fours, regenerating any wound that fire or acid has not seared. It stinks of the bog and hits like a falling tree. It is too stupid to fear and too durable to ignore. Mire-folk keep oil and flint within reach at all times.

entries.title: Hydra
entries.flavour: A many-headed reptilian horror, the hydra wallows in The Mire's deepest pools, each serpentine neck striking on its own and snapping at anything in reach. It cannot be frightened, and it bites back the instant something draws near. Cut a head away and it simply works with the others. It is the apex even the crocodiles fear.

entries.title: Blackwater Wight
entries.flavour: The drowned dead given malice, the blackwater wight is a barnacled corpse-warrior that rises from the mire's black pools, hauling the recently dead up behind it. Its blade drinks the life from those it cuts, and the wound will not fully close until the adventure ends. It commands the drowned the way a sergeant commands recruits. The mire's deepest channels are its barracks.

entries.title: Mire Titan
entries.flavour: A colossal amphibian-horror, the mire titan is a froglike bulk of warty hide and lashing tentacles crowned by a vast, distensible maw. It seizes prey in its arms and swallows them whole, dissolving them in its acid gut while they still struggle. It is The Mire's living sinkhole. Whole expeditions have gone into one and left only ripples.
entries.direction: A typical Mire Titan alone, waist-deep in fen water, reeds and mud sliding from its body; no geodes or hunters.

entries.title: Black Dragon
entries.flavour: The Mire's sovereign, the black dragon is a sleek, horned wyrm the colour of stagnant water, its breath a hiss of acid. Cruel and patient, it lairs in a flooded ruin and rules the fen through terror, taking tribute and tearing apart any who refuse to pay. It swims as easily as it flies. When the frogs go silent and the water stills, it is already close.
entries.direction: A typical adult black dragon rising from open black water, acid dripping from its jaws; no ruin or architecture.

entries.title: The Ancient Void Dragon
entries.flavour: Older than the Fall and perhaps its cause, the Ancient Void Dragon is a wound in the shape of a wyrm, its scales drinking the light from the air around them. Its breath neither burns nor freezes but unmakes, peeling away substance until nothing is left. Stars seem to dim where it passes. The wise do not speak its name, and the dead do not speak at all.
entries.direction: The Ancient Void Dragon drawn mostly as negative space: a wyrm-shaped absence edged by fine lines, stars dimming around it.

entries.title: The Hollow Crown of the Ashlands
entries.flavour: The empire's last emperor died without an heir, and the crown itself took up the rule. A circlet of black iron hovering above an empty regent's robe, the Hollow Crown commands the Ashlands' legions with a dead sovereign's absolute authority. It passes judgement that withers the living and raises the fallen to enforce it. Its throne room is the whole of the ruined empire.
entries.direction: A black iron circlet floating above an empty regent's robe on a ruined throne, ranks of dead legionaries kneeling below.

entries.title: The Last Colossus
entries.flavour: A walking fortress of riveted black iron three times a man's height, the Last Colossus groans at every joint with the thunder bound inside it. When the empire knew it was dying, it poured the last of its wealth into one war-construct meant to outlast everything. For centuries it has marched the same patrol, defending an empire that no longer exists. Nothing has yet proven able to stop it.
entries.direction: A riveted black-iron war-construct three times a man's height marching along a ruined imperial road, a small figure at its feet for scale.

entries.title: Avatar of the Old Growth
entries.flavour: A towering shape of ancient trunk and grasping root, bark-skinned and crowned with a tangle of antlered branches, the Avatar of the Old Growth is the will of the deep forest given a body to act through. It calls the lesser green things to its side and drowns intruders in living wood. To kill it is to wound the Greenmark itself. The Greenmark does not forgive.
entries.direction: A colossal walking tree-giant towering over the forest canopy, roots dragging behind it, its crown a tangle of antlered branches.

entries.title: The Broodmother Prime
entries.flavour: In the deepest dark of the Undermarches squats the mother of every giant spider that plagues the deep, a bloated horror the size of a cottage, egg-sacs trailing from it that twitch with the unborn. It floods the field with its brood and binds the survivors in webs for later. Its venom stops a heart in a single beat. The deep, in the end, is its nursery.
entries.direction: The Broodmother squatting in a vast webbed cavern, cottage-sized, egg-sacs trailing, cocooned victims hanging in the webs.

entries.title: Captain Veyr of the Forsaken
entries.flavour: Veyr was the empire's greatest captain, who swore their company would never break and held them to it past death itself.
