Now they lead the Forsaken in spectral plate, a duelist whose paired blades have not slowed in three centuries. They rally their dead soldiers with a voice like a closing tomb. They no longer recall the war they are still fighting. Only the oath.
entries.direction: Captain Veyr in spectral plate with paired blades raised, rallying a line of dead soldiers behind them.

entries.title: The Frost Bailiff Magistrate
entries.flavour: The Pale City's court needed an enforcer for the sentences its living judges feared to sign, and so it raised one of its own into something colder still. The Frost Bailiff Magistrate drifts the frozen avenues passing final judgement, freezing the guilty where they stand and calling the White Court to carry out the verdict. Its rulings cannot be appealed. Its sentences are always death.
entries.direction: The Frost Bailiff drifting down a frozen avenue in judicial robes, a figure freezing solid where they stand before it.

entries.title: The Sun-Crowned Prince
entries.flavour: The greatest of the priest-kings refused to let their reign end and bound their soul into a crown of beaten gold. A wrapped and withered corpse robed in funeral linen, the crown still bright above a face of leather and bone, the Sun-Crowned Prince rules their sealed tomb-court as they ruled in life. They raise their skeletal subjects and scour trespassers with decrees of searing flame. They still believe the world answers to them, and within their tomb it does.
entries.direction: The Sun-Crowned Prince enthroned in a sealed tomb-court, a withered corpse in funeral linen beneath a bright crown of beaten gold.

entries.title: The Antlered Warden of the Tithe
entries.flavour: The antlered figure admitted to Greythorn's west gate each winter does not come to bargain when the tithe goes unpaid. It comes to collect. A towering shape of bone-antler and living wood, it drags the indebted into its reach and calls the wild court to witness. The forest has never broken the agreement, and it does not forgive those who do.
entries.direction: A gaunt, man-sized-to-towering figure of bone-antler and living wood standing at Greythorn's west gate in winter snow, dragging a debtor by the collar.

entries.title: The Voice Beneath the Bells
entries.flavour: Survivors describe a small figure at the edge of the torchlight, singing in a tongue that sounds like an old lullaby heard through water. Then the torch goes out. The Voice Beneath the Bells is grief given a child's shape and a drowned chapel's patience, and its song hollows out everyone who hears it. The bells it waits beneath have not rung in a very long time.
entries.direction: A small child-shaped figure at the edge of guttering torchlight in a flooded chapel, singing, the bells hanging silent above.

entries.title: Maelthorn the Verdant
entries.flavour: Maelthorn is a vast wyrm the deep green of stagnant pondwater, its overlapping scales furred with moss and creeping lichen. It does not hunt, because the Greenmark hunts on its behalf, and Greythorn sends the autumn tithe in place of a war party. Its breath is a rolling fog of poison that wilts all it touches. When it finally stirs, the lesser beasts of the wood flee the grove ahead of it.
entries.direction: Maelthorn coiled in a forest clearing among Greythorn's autumn tithe offerings, moss and lichen furring its scales, poison fog spilling from its jaws.

entries.title: Sirrach the Black
entries.flavour: Sirrach is the Undermarches' buried king, a black wyrm that swims through solid stone and surfaces only to feed. Its breath withers flesh and shortens lives, leaving even survivors diminished. It hoards in galleries no surface-dweller has ever mapped. The stone shudders before it the way a hand shudders before opening bad news.
entries.direction: Sirrach erupting out of solid stone in an unmapped gallery, the rock rippling like water around its black body.

entries.title: Visath the White
entries.flavour: Visath is the Pale City's eternal winter wearing the body of a wyrm, a glacier with wings and a will. Its breath does not merely freeze; it stops time in the flesh, leaving victims locked mid-scream in the ice. It rules from the highest spire and suffers no warmth anywhere in its domain. Where it flies, the snow falls harder, as though the sky itself bows.
entries.direction: Visath perched atop the highest frozen spire of the Pale City, wings spread, victims locked mid-scream in the ice below.

entries.title: Khorrun the Dracolich
entries.flavour: Khorrun has not drawn breath since the Fall, yet still it coils atop its hoard in the sealed tomb-galleries beneath the Sun-Drowned. Its bones hold the shape of greed, draped in the tatters of scale and the cold blue fire of undeath, and ledgers stacked to the vault ceiling record exactly who has taken what. It rouses only to punish a debt or devour a trespasser. The lightning that pours from its jaws is the same colour as the witchfire in its empty sockets.
entries.direction: Khorrun's skeletal dragon body draped in tattered scale, coiled atop a hoard in a tomb gallery, ledgers stacked to the ceiling.

entries.title: Vossegar of the Flooded Cathedral
entries.flavour: Vossegar lairs in a drowned cathedral at The Mire's heart, a sleek black wyrm coiled among submerged altars. Its acid breath strips flesh from bone, and at its will the waters rise to swallow the ground its enemies stand on. It takes tribute from every settlement in the mire and devours those who come up short. The bells of its cathedral toll underwater, and the frogs have not sung there in living memory.
entries.direction: Vossegar coiled among submerged altars and broken pillars inside a drowned cathedral, black water rising around the nave.

entries.title: Scenario 1: Hunt the Wild Beast
entries.flavour: Something out of the deep wood has taken Greythorn's logging camps for its hunting ground, and with them the timber the Bastion is built on. The first deaths were blamed on dire wolves. The next were found driven through splintered palisade timbers, which dire wolves do not manage. Its pelt, skull, and teeth would buy a season behind the walls, and the Council of Captains will pay either way to have the camps cutting again. Comfort and timber have sent both parties into the trees.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Whispering Grove
entries.flavour: The grove is older than Greythorn and older than the western forest road that skirts it. The standing stones hum when no wind passes, and pale lights move between them on moonless nights. Greythorn's farmers leave bread there and do not look back. Scholars call it a site of power. The Council of Captains calls it part of the tithe, and pays it without complaint.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Bandit's Toll
entries.flavour: The western forest road carries Deepwarden iron, Reedmarch salt, and grain between the Bastions, and it is the one artery Greythorn cannot do without. A toll crew has claimed a bend of the trail and nailed its prices to the trees in stolen blood. Caravans wait behind palisades while bread grows dear inside Greythorn's walls. The Council of Captains has stamped a bounty and sent it out with anyone hungry enough to answer.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Spider's Silk Route
entries.flavour: Silk-traders whisper of a ravine in the deep Greenmark where the webs hold steel like thread and fetch absurd prices in Bastion markets. The spinners are the Broodmother's daughters, strayed up from the dark, and the place is on no honest map. That has not stopped a Greythorn merchant from selling the same path through the thorns to two parties at once.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Ambushed Emissary
entries.flavour: An emissary vanished on the western forest road carrying documents sealed under two rival Bastion laws. One patron in Greythorn wants the courier found breathing. Another, further off, wants the satchel and does not ask after the courier. The deep wood has kept worse secrets, and the Hollow Quarter is not telling.

entries.title: Scenario 6: Ritual of the Old Growth
entries.flavour: An Old Growth elder works slowly over a sickness in the roots, and a Heartwood Totem worth more than most villages stands at the heart of the rite. Greythorn's tithe forbids touching it, and the Council of Captains keeps the tithe because the alternative is the wild court at the gate. Another Bastion, with no forest to answer to, calls the same act salvage. The roots are listening to both.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Fallen Observatory
entries.flavour: A star-engine once crowned these ruins, and its broken brass arms still turn when moonlight enters the cracked dome. Wizards would give a finger for the instruments scattered across the shifting floors, which is precisely why the Sable Watch wants them carried to Sablekeep and locked away from unregistered hands. The old servants of the place still know the penalty for touching them. They have a great deal of time in which to enforce it.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Guardian's Test
entries.flavour: A sealed gate dominates the courtyard, black with soot and old prayers, somewhere along the imperial roads that run out from the dead empire's heart. The texts say a vault waits beyond. They warn that worthiness is tested before entry, and no surviving copy explains what worthiness means. The Sable Watch insists the guardian answers to a seal nobody now holds, while a rival party arrives carrying a Hollow Crown's Writ and a very different opinion.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Shifting Sands of Time
entries.flavour: The ruin does not keep time honestly. Glyphs flare and gutter. Soot drifts uphill in the corners. Stone that bore a traveller's weight at dawn may open beneath them by noon. Relics surface when the place remembers them and sink before anyone can make a clean claim, and the Sable Watch will register whatever is carried back to Sablekeep, whether the finder wishes it registered or not.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Sealed Archive
entries.flavour: A sealed archive lies under a fractured basilica in the dead empire's heart: tablets, scrolls, debt records, and sermons the Sable Watch would rather see burned than read. Dust chokes the corridors. Scavengers have gnawed through the newer shelves. Something older keeps the inner stacks in order, and it has waited longer than Sablekeep has stood for someone to disturb them.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Reliquary of Broken Saints
entries.flavour: Broken statues and smashed reliquaries fill the hall, and sanctified bone and silver remain in the wreckage, too holy to abandon and too valuable to leave. Sablekeep needs the relics to keep its braziers lit and its authority legal, and will pay to register every fragment. The dead here are not confused. They swore to guard these relics, and death has not released them from the oath.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Iron-Vein Vault
entries.flavour: The vault has been sealed for two generations. Karnessa Iron-Vein pressed their blood into the iron door when something inside began to leak through the walls, and the seal has held. Until now. Tremors along the imperial roads have cracked the outer binding, and something below is pushing. Sablekeep sends one party to reinforce the seal before whatever waits finishes its work; a rival patron sends another to open the vault and price what was sealed there. The vault does not care about either contract.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Crystal Harvest
entries.flavour: A new cavern has opened beneath the broken mountains, and its crystal veins pulse with cold light and drag iron filings across the floor. Deepwarden's forges would trade a season of grain for a vein this clean. The prospectors who found it have already lied about its location, and both parties arrive before the lie can harden into a map.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Chasm Crossing
entries.flavour: A chasm splits the caverns like a wound in the world, crossed only by narrow ledges in broken pieces. A Survey Map must reach the Lantern Council before Deepwarden's rivals can claim the new diggings. Things cling to the dark stone below the ledges and wait for a hand to shake. The Council wants the map. It does not ask what the things want.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Quake
entries.flavour: The old tunnels shook themselves open before dawn, and gemstone veins glimmer where the support beams snapped. Aftershocks still run through the stone. Deepwarden wants the gems hauled out before the shafts settle, and the usual exits are already blocked. The Dark has noticed the new air, and it is not the only thing moving toward it.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Undermarches Outpost Raid
entries.flavour: Scouts found an outpost below an old road shrine and did not stay to count the banners. Plans for a surface incursion lie inside, and so does the officer who drew them. Deepwarden wants the plans more than it wants the credit, and two parties descend under separate seals, each ordered to take the plans and claim the victory before the other can sell it.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Shadowed Under Passage
entries.flavour: This passage has been touched by a colder dark than stone can explain. Breath sounds wrong here. The shadows lie against the light instead of with it. A Heart of Shadow waits below, prized by those who bargain with the deep elves and feared by anyone who has read Deepwarden's old warnings. The Lantern Council would rather it stayed lost. Someone with coin disagrees.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Ritual of Shadow Binding
entries.flavour: In a cavern without honest light, deep elf priests have drawn a binding circle around something that answers from the dark below the Dark. One patron in Deepwarden wants the rite broken before it finishes. Another wants the circle lifted out intact, sigils and all, and will not say for whom. The thing inside the circle has not been consulted.

entries.title: Scenario 1: Plunder of the Frozen Ruins
entries.flavour: The Pale City is littered with magical treasure because its people froze too quickly to hide it, and Hearthhold has lived for generations by thawing out what they left. A promising ruin has cracked open under the snow. Both parties enter before the frozen citizens notice another room has been disturbed, because the citizens do notice, eventually, and they do not forgive trespass.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Alchemist's Frozen Laboratory
entries.flavour: In the ice-locked Silent District, north along the road out of Hearthhold, an alchemist's laboratory remains sealed under frost. The formula inside might be worth a village, and Hearthhold burns through everything it owns just to stay warm. The cold has preserved the benches, the bottles, the last mistakes, and the guardians left to watch them. Some things in that laboratory were never meant to thaw.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Haunted Mausoleum
entries.flavour: The mausoleum stands under the ice with its doors still sealed, and a noble family of the White Court rests below, or pretends to. Their heirlooms remain in the crypt, polished by cold and watched by names too proud to fade. Hearthhold needs whatever can be sold to buy another winter's fuel. The Court does not recognize the sale.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Clockwork Menagerie
entries.flavour: A Deepwarden tinker came north chasing a commission and froze here with the rest of the city, and the workshop is full of brass legs, biting gears, and small minds wound tight around old orders. The tinker is dust. The orders remain. Hearthhold's fire-watch wants the intact cores and the notebooks explaining how not to die retrieving them, because a Bastion this poor cannot leave brass that still moves.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Ice Wyrm's Hoard
entries.flavour: The old stories put jewels and gold in a frozen cavern beneath the north road out of Hearthhold, and a wyrm coiled on top of them whose breath can stop a heart inside its own armour. Hearthhold needs the gold more than it fears the breath, which is the kind of arithmetic only the poorest Bastion does out loud. The second part of the story has never discouraged the first kind of listener.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Icebound Court
entries.flavour: An ice-bound court still convenes in a sanctum of blue glass and frozen banners, north of every fire Hearthhold keeps lit. Its ruler is the Frost Bailiff Magistrate, who keeps bound spirits and carved servants close and passes sentences that were old before Hearthhold was founded. At the centre of the chamber lies the Heartfrost Shard, cold enough to make breath sound like prayer. Hearthhold wants the Shard. The Magistrate has not adjourned.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Oasis Raiders
entries.flavour: A vital oasis south of the mountain passes has changed hands again, and raiders hold the wells, the shade, and the people too slow to flee. Saltspire sells water as sovereignty, and an oasis it does not control is a debt it cannot collect. One contract from the Well-Keepers says liberation. A rival contract says seizure. The water will not ask which seal is righteous.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Cinder Lord's Lost Brazier
entries.flavour: A brass brazier lies somewhere in the scorched ruins, still holding the ember of a bound Cinder Lord. The relic promises power to the hand that completes the binding, and Saltspire knows more about binding infernal things to contracts than it admits to anyone. One patron wants the brazier brought in quietly. Another wants the binding finished out here. Promises made by fire should be read twice.

entries.title: Scenario 3: Tomb of the Sunken Kings
entries.flavour: The sand has drawn back from a tomb complex of the priest-kings, and gilded chambers show through the heat shimmer. The old hazards remain patient, and so do the guardians. Saltspire will buy whatever is carried out and ask no awkward questions about how, because plausible innocence is worth as much to it as gold. Nothing buried with a priest-king expects to be taken politely.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Sandwyrm's Lair
entries.flavour: Nomad legends speak of a vast shape beneath the dunes south of the passes, and a gullet lined with the treasure of everything it has swallowed. The nomads tell it as a warning. Saltspire's patrons hear it as an inventory and pay accordingly. The dunes do not distinguish between the two kinds of listener.

entries.title: Scenario 5: The Cursed Colossus of the Waste
entries.flavour: A colossal statue of a priest-king rises from the sand, broken at the waist and still angry, with a Heartstone lodged in its hollow chest. Fortune-hunters call it a prize. Grave-robbers know better and come anyway, and Saltspire pays the survivors of either trade the same rate. The waste keeps the ones who do not survive.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Cinder Lord's Obsidian Prison
entries.flavour: An obsidian dais burns without fuel at the centre of the ruin, and a Cinder Lord strains against the binding that holds it. Saltspire's Well-Keepers wrote bindings like this one, back when the desert still kept its own law, and one of them wants the prison strengthened before it fails. A rival patron wants it broken and calls that ambition. The Cinder Lord calls it overdue.

entries.title: Scenario 1: The Reliquary of Edrava Salttide
entries.flavour: Recent floods opened a grave-house that The Mire had kept sealed for two hundred years. Edrava Salttide, the salt-coast's last great toll-lord, who fed their enemies to the tide and married four pirate-kings in succession, was laid here with a reliquary no Bastion will admit to wanting and every Bastion has quietly sent parties to find. Reedmarch knew where it lay all along and sold the location twice. Both parties enter before the dead gather the strength to close the door again. The water smells of salt. There is no ocean for eighty miles.

entries.title: Scenario 2: The Lizardfolk's Stolen Offerings
entries.flavour: A lizardfolk shrine in the deep fen was raided before dawn, and the Sunstone Amulet and the offering-piles were dragged off into the reeds. The lizardfolk temple-guards want it back, and they remember faces. One writ names the amulet sacred and to be returned. Another names the silver recoverable property, and Reedmarch will broker either errand for its usual cut of silence.

entries.title: Scenario 3: The Mire Titan's Fen
entries.flavour: A Mire Titan has claimed the bubbling fen, and glimmering geodes lie scattered through its territory like bait, because that is more or less what they are. Hunters arrive with hooks, ropes, and prayers. Thieves arrive lighter and usually leave that way. Reedmarch wants the geodes and does not much care which trade brings them in, so long as the fen stays quiet about the rest.

entries.title: Scenario 4: The Blighted Heartwood
entries.flavour: Blight has wrapped the swamp growth around a pulsing Heartwood that beats under the bark like a buried organ. One patron wants it destroyed before the rot spreads to the ferry-roads Reedmarch lives on. Another wants its corruption bottled and carried off, and neither wants to be the one holding it on the way home. The Marsh Council would prefer the whole matter stay unspoken.

entries.title: Scenario 5: Salttide's Reckoning
entries.flavour: A curse lies over the sacred island like oil on water. Edrava Salttide has made a ritual of the place, the same ritual they once used to curse the harbours that refused their ships, now turned on the living who entered The Mire without paying the toll. The reeds bend toward the island. The water smells of brine, this far from any sea. Reedmarch sent one party to break the working, and let a rival sell the other a contract whose small print it has not read.

entries.title: Scenario 6: The Serpent's Sunken Hoard
entries.flavour: A flooded sinkhole has opened in the black water, and something ancient coils below it, older than Reedmarch's oldest ferry-family. Its hide, its hoard, and its death would each command a price in a different market. The water is dark enough to hide which one is being hunted, and Reedmarch prefers it that way. Whatever is down there has paid the toll longer than anyone alive, and does not intend to stop now.

entries.title: 11.1 Campaign Overview
entries.flavour: A Stronghold is not a castle in the noble sense. No ancient bloodline sanctifies it. No bard remembers its founding. It is a claim driven into a dying world with coin, fear, salvage, and stubborn labour. Its stones come from ruined shrines, abandoned watch-keeps, broken bridges, and walls that failed other people first. Its gates are paid for with burial gold, bounty coin, chapel debt, and the last wages of the dead.
entries.direction: A stronghold under construction from salvage: workers hauling shrine stones and broken bridge spans up a ramp, scaffolding around a half-built keep.

entries.title: The Vault
entries.flavour: The Vault is not a treasury. It is a sealed confession of greed, iron-bound and watched by clerks who sleep in shifts. They count each coin as if the dead might come back to collect.
entries.direction: A low iron-bound vault room; a clerk dozing on a stool beside chests and coin scales while a second clerk counts by candle.

entries.title: The Barracks
entries.flavour: The Barracks smell of straw, old sweat, damp wool, and boiled leather. Names are carved into the beams by people who expected to return. Few are still spoken.
entries.direction: Rows of straw bunks under heavy beams carved with names; damp wool and boots hung to dry; one empty bunk with a helmet left on it.

entries.title: The Armoury
entries.flavour: The Armoury smells of oil, wet leather, coal smoke, and old violence. Its walls hold blades recovered from drowned shrines, shields hammered flat after dragon-fire, and helms whose former owners are better left unnamed.
entries.direction: Racks of salvaged arms: blades from drowned shrines, a shield hammered flat by dragon-fire, ownerless helms on pegs, an oil-cloth bench.

entries.title: The Apothecary
entries.flavour: The Apothecary is built around heat, glass, knives, bone saws, and the bitter stink of herbs that should not grow in clean soil. Its shelves hold tinctures from The Mire, salts from the Sun-Drowned, and poultices learned from surgeons paid in secrets.
entries.direction: A cramped workroom of glass alembics over a brazier, bone saws and knives on a cloth, shelves of labelled-less jars and hanging bitter herbs.

entries.title: The Outer Walls
entries.flavour: The Outer Walls declare that the dark must work harder. Stone, timber, ditch, spike, and warding nail stand between the party's claim and the things that circle after sundown.
entries.direction: The stronghold's ditch, spiked palisade and stone wall at night, warding nails driven into the timbers, a lone sentry with a torch on the walkway.

entries.title: The Arcanum
entries.flavour: The Arcanum rises too thin and too tall. Its upper windows burn at hours when honest fires should be dead. Brass instruments turn toward storms, old constellations, and places where the sky has not healed.
entries.direction: A thin, too-tall tower against a night sky, upper windows burning, brass instruments on its roof turned toward a storm.

entries.title: The Stronghold Chapel
entries.flavour: The Chapel is small, cold, and crowded with votive offerings from those who survived by inches. Its saints are chipped. Its relics are suspect. Its candles burn low even when no wind enters.
entries.direction: A small cold chapel crowded with votive offerings, chipped saint statues and low candles, a single mourner kneeling.

entries.title: The War Room
entries.flavour: The War Room is where contracts are signed, debts are denied, and maps are stained. Its hearth burns beneath banners taken from ruins, enemies, and dead patrons.
entries.direction: A heavy table under captured banners, stained maps pinned with knives, a contract and quill, a hearth burning behind.

entries.title: The Expedition Hall
entries.flavour: The Expedition Hall is packed earth, split posts, blunted steel, blood in the mud, and shouted correction from veterans with no patience for heroic stupidity. New recruits learn quickly that courage is not a defence.
entries.direction: A packed-earth training yard inside split-post walls: a scarred veteran correcting a recruit's guard, blunted weapons on a rack, mud underfoot.

entries.title: The Undercroft
entries.flavour: The Undercroft is a warren of cellars, sealed drains, hidden doors, and passages older than the Stronghold above it. Smugglers, informants, and quiet killers all find reasons to know its shape.
entries.direction: A vaulted cellar warren lit by one lantern, a hidden door ajar, a cloaked figure slipping into an older passage below.

entries.title: A.4 Quickstart Scenario: The Broken Courier
entries.flavour: A royal courier was cut down on the old road. The satchel still lies beside the body, and a small lockbox has been thrown clear into the brush. Both parties race to seize the dispatches before wolves or rivals claim them.
